newsitem.title: CANADA: Commodity prices, Bre-X seen driving Canada oils.
newsitem.headline: Commodity prices, Bre-X seen driving Canada oils.

text.p: Canadian oil and gas stocks are staging a big return to investor favor as strong commodity prices and an exodus from golds in the wake of the Bre-X Minerals Ltd scandal push up prices, analysts said.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's oil and gas subindex was up 88.98 points on Friday to 6,647.24, up nearly 600 points from a recent low of 6,053.62 on April 11.
At the time, analysts were concerned that a correction among oil stocks would be prolonged after the subindex rose to an all-time high of 6,927.89 in January, then ebbed.

Several companies were enjoying big gains late in Friday's session, including Alberta Energy Co Ltd, which was up 1.10 to 31.50, Renaissance Energy Ltd up 0.90 to 39.60, Suncor Energy Inc up 0.95 to 35.50 and Anderson Exploration Ltd up 0.50 to 18.50.
Peter Linder, analyst with CIBC Wood Gundy, said recent strength in both oil and natural gas prices as well as a spate of stellar first-quarter results were bolstering share prices in the sector.
The exodus of investors from Canada's gold sector as uncertainty began to circulate over the amount of gold at Bre-X's Busang property in Indonesia helped too, Linder said.
"I think the fallout from Bre-X has caused some people who still want to be in the resource sector to look more toward the oils," he said.
The Calgary-based prospector was devastated by news early this week that its property held no gold and that Busang appeared to be the biggest mining scam in history.
Linder said the combination of factors working in the oil sector's favor could continue for the next few months and move cash flow multiples upward.

NYMEX West Texas Intermediate crude oil closed up US9 cents on Friday to US$20.43 per barrel, while Henry Hub natural gas futures remained seasonally strong, closing at US$2.242 per million British thermal units.
Canadian natural gas prices at the AECO storage Hub in Alberta were quoted in the mid-C$1.70s per gigajoule, down about 8 cents on the day, but still high compared to spring prices in previous years.
